chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Max the Mayor's Brooklyn club, checkrooms and how Price made a living
summary: He shows a Brooklyn owner how to keep inventory in exchange for the band and checkroom, and explains how he survived in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: But the show closed, and after that I went to 52nd Street, and I went back to the Café Society. And then we opened a place in Brooklyn and I had the band out there with Max the Mayor. Do you know Max the Mayor? He didn't understand the quart system. He didn't understand...I had to show him and his partner how to take an inventory on their whiskey. You know, they just...you know, the bartender just poured like that they didn't know the difference... and then/they didn't know what was left...they'd just take all the bottles and put them in the back and then when...and set them back on the bar and pour it out and no kind of inventory record. So I showed them... 'Hey Max, how many bottles of whiskey you got? Twenty? Okay. How many you putting out on the bar? Twenty. Okay, put out ten. Put ten in reserve, then check on the bottles, see what's left and, you know, estimate what the remaining amount of whiskey's left in the bottle. How many cans of...' They'd just have a whole lot of cans of beer or bottles of beer, and just have it stacked up with a whole lot of iced soda and sell it and, you know, half the bottles gone and they don't know from nothing. Plus I had the band.

Now in exchange for me doing that, what I did for him to help him, he gave me the band and he let me have the checkroom. Well, I was always all right with...these people were supposed to be underworld people, or gangsters, or whatever they were...I didn't know. But I always...I could get checkrooms. You know, so this is how I'm making a living.

God, I don't know how I'm making a living. I'm driving a big car, you know, checkrooms, see me eat in the better places with everybody; see me at the fight, ringside; go to Chicago, you know, when Sugar Ray fought Jake LaMotta or whoever he fought; here at Joe Louis', you know; go to the Polo Grounds, Madison Square Garden, then I knew everybody. And I knew everybody. Because of the fact that many of these people who I knew in the territories (and) in the various cities, if they were not living in New York, they'd come here. And when they'd come here they'd look me up. So guys just could not figure that out. So that's how I survived over the years. That's how I survived.
Once I almost had a meat company, you know. Down Home...
